title: How many pages are still left to read?
description: A novel of four hundred pages is read in two parts, one fifth yesterday and three tenths today. The two fractions are added with a common denominator, taken from one whole, and the part left is turned into pages.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the parts read, take that from the whole to get the part left, then find that part of the pages. Watch for students who take one fifth and three tenths from four hundred as if they were pages.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): Leeza is reading a novel that has 400 pages. Leeza read 1/5 of the pages yesterday and 3/10 today. How many more pages are left to read?
video_script.why: A learner adds fractions of a whole, finds the part left, and takes that part of the pages.
video_script.substitution: the book's own novel of four hundred pages and the parts read on two days
video_script.anchor: a novel of four hundred pages drawn as one bar
video_script.payoff_line: Leeza still has two hundred pages to read.
video_script.fraction_reading: one fifth, three tenths, two tenths, five tenths, one half

names.Leeza: the person who reads a novel of 400 pages

video_script.design: One bar for the whole novel, with a shaded part for each day; the working band adds the parts, takes them from one, and turns the rest into pages.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a novel drawn as one long bar of four hundred pages with two shaded parts

marks.yest: the one fifth part is shaded
marks.today: the three tenths part is shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about Leeza and a novel.
The novel has four hundred pages.
<bookmark mark='yest'/>Leeza read one fifth of the pages yesterday.
<bookmark mark='today'/>Today Leeza read three tenths of the pages.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many more pages are left to finish the novel?

beats.on_screen: the bar stays on the board; Keeko sits beside it

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the bar cut into ten equal parts; one fifth shown as two of them

marks.ten: the bar is cut into ten equal parts
marks.whole: the whole bar is marked as one

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Cut the novel into ten equal parts.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>One fifth of the novel is the same as two of these tenths.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>The part read and the part left together make the whole novel, which is one.

beats.on_screen: Given: 400 pages; read 1/5 yesterday and 3/10 today

marks.given: the pages and the two fractions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a novel of four hundred pages, with one fifth read yesterday and three tenths read today.

beats.on_screen: To find: pages left to read

marks.find: the words pages left are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many pages are left to read.

marks.add: one fifth plus three tenths is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, the part read is one fifth plus three tenths.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The denominators differ, so we write one fifth as two tenths.

marks.add: the numerators two and three are added over ten
marks.low: five tenths is reduced to one half

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the numerators, two plus three, over the same denominator ten.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Five tenths in lowest form is one half.

marks.left: one minus one half is written and the unshaded half lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, the part left is the whole take away the part read.
That is one take away one half, which is one half.

marks.pages: one half times four hundred is written

narration: <bookmark mark='pages'/>Step four, the pages left are one half of four hundred, one half times four hundred.

marks.check: the pages read each day are written and added to the pages left

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check with the pages read.
One fifth of four hundred is eighty, and three tenths of four hundred is one hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Leeza still has two hundred pages to read.
Eighty, one hundred twenty and two hundred make the four hundred pages of the novel.
